subject: Inference tail-latency hit — remediation request & credit calculation for MalloryPay
body:
From: Alyssa Morgan <alyssa@mallorypay.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: ops@mallorypay.com
Date: Fri, 10 Feb 2028 10:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Sustained tail-latency observed 2028-02-09 21:00-23:45 UTC — request for remediation & credit

Hi Stephanie,

We saw a sustained tail-latency regression in our checkout inference calls on 2028-02-09 between ~21:00 and 23:45 UTC. 12% of generation requests spiked above our SLA target (p95 > 1.2s, p99 > 2.8s) and our error budget was significantly impacted during the Black Friday weekend run. Attached are a short pcap of representative traffic and our local SLO snapshot.

Can you confirm whether this maps to an incident on your side, provide an official incident window, and outline eligibility for a service credit? We also need a postmortem and an ETA for a remediation/action plan.

This affected MalloryPay production (tenant id MW-PROD-19). Please loop in whoever owns SLA adjudications.

Thanks,
Alyssa Morgan
Head of Site Reliability
MalloryPay

Team — MalloryPay reports a p99 tail during 2028-02-09 21:00-23:45 UTC. Please action the following before EOD PST:
- Aditya: pull serving traces (kv-cache hits, model variant fallbacks, quantized CPU fallbacks), host-level telemetry, and any autoscaler events for that window.
- David: generate SLO burn report for MW-PROD-19 for the 90-day lookback and isolate 2028-02-09 window; start provisional credit calc.

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 11 Feb 2028 09:43:37 -08:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: MalloryPay tail-latency — initial findings

Folks — preliminary findings from runtime side:
- We observed a warmup storm in US-WEST-2 edge pool that coincided with a large model variant rollout in the 20:50–21:30 UTC range. Several client requests were routed to a hot path that triggered a fallback to an older quantized CPU instance group when GPU pool capacity temporarily dropped.
- Consequence: KV cache miss amplification and CPU-bound generation increased p99 from ~0.7s to ~2.9s for a sustained sub-window of ~37 minutes. Our telemetry shows ~12% of MalloryPay's requests in that window had >1.5s latency.
- Attached: packet clip and SLO snapshot reproduce the spike. Autoscaler logs show 3 back-to-back preemption events and a transient scheduling backlog at 20:58 UTC.

Suggested immediate mitigation: reserve a dedicated warm pool for tenant bursts (short term), and adjust autoscaler grace-time for mixed-tenant GPU pools (medium term).

Provisional credit calc (preliminary): using contractual SLA (99.9% uptime for p99 <= 1s) and observed burn, estimated credit = 3.2% monthly invoice prorated for affected window. David, please confirm.

-Aditya
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime

---

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Morgan <alyssa@mallorypay.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 08:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Redwood incident confirmation and provisional remediation/credit for 2028-02-09 tail-latency

Hi Alyssa — thank you for your patience. Below is our formal response and next steps: 

1) Incident confirmation and window
   - Confirmed incident window: 2028-02-09 20:50 UTC — 2028-02-09 21:27 UTC (37 minutes). During this window we observed concurrency-driven warmup and temporary fallback to CPU-quantized model variant for a subset of requests routed through the US-WEST-2 edge pool.

2) Impact summary
   - Affected customer tenant: MalloryPay (MW-PROD-19).
   - Observed effect: p99 latency increased to ~2.9s; ~12% of requests exceeded 1.5s. No increased error rate (5xx) was observed, but latency breach triggered SLA exposure.

3) Provisional credit calculation
   - Per contract SLA and our accounting: provisional credit = 3.2% of the monthly invoice for MalloryPay, apportioned to the affected window. This is provisional pending David's final reconciliation and legal sign-off. Attached is our working calc (provisional_credit_calc_20280211.xlsx).

4) Remediation and mitigations
   - Short term (next 48 hours): reserve a short-lived warm pool for MalloryPay bursts; manual pinning of critical routes to GPU-backed model variants. Scheduled maintenance to apply autoscaler grace-time patch.
   - Medium term: autoscaler policy changes, improved fallback thresholds, and improved rollout gating for model variants across mixed-tenant pools.

5) Postmortem and meeting
   - We'd like to schedule a 60-minute postmortem with MalloryPay week of Feb 20. Proposed times: Tue Feb 21 17:00 UTC or Wed Feb 22 15:00 UTC. Please confirm preferred slot.

6) Evidence & transparency
   - Raw telemetry and logs have been uploaded: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bMalloryIncident
   - HubSpot record: https://hubspot.com/contacts/record/HS-448122

Next steps: David will finalize the credit computation and legal will issue a formal remediation letter. Laura will draft the customer-facing postmortem. Aditya and runtime will document the rollout gating change and autoscaler patch schedule.

Please reply with approval for the provisional credit and preferred time for the postmortem.

Best regards,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference
